summary: Yakama Reservation lookout: a 1935 wooden tower, then a 68-foot Aermotor tower moved from Panther Creek in 1964; access by Yakama Nation tour only.

facts.design: 68-foot all-steel Aermotor tower, moved here from Panther Creek in 1964

access.note: On Yakama Reservation land, closed to the public. Willhite gives access as restricted, by Yakama Nation tour only. The 2019 visits were tribal tours arranged with the Yakama Nation.

visit.trail_note: The sources describe only tribal tours, not public visits. Ask the Yakama Nation before planning any visit.

events.note: First lookout: a pole tower with a tent camp.
A three-legged, 55-foot wooden tower with an 8-by-8-foot cab and ground house replaced the 1920 pole tower.
A December 1940 Goldendale newspaper item reported two lookouts sending twice-daily short-wave radio reports to the Satus Pass station.
A 68-foot Aermotor steel tower was moved here from Panther Creek and replaced the 1935 wooden tower.
The Yakama Nation gave a small group a spring and a fall guided tour in exchange for volunteer help to open and close a lookout for the season.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on April 13, 2022.

corrections.why: 2.4 m is about the 8-foot width of the 1935 cab, not a tower height. The sources describe a 68-foot Aermotor tower, about 20.7 m. They do not give the cab floor height, so an editor should confirm the value before it is used.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1935 date is the wooden tower, which the register gives as built in 1935. The lookout standing today is the 68-foot tower moved here in 1964, so both dates are right for different structures.
The register gives 5,103 ft (1,555 m) and TrailChick and firelookout.com give 5,100 ft. The record's 1555.4 m matches the register.

sources.title: Signal Peak Fire Lookout, Yakama Nation

notes_for_editor: Access is by Yakama Nation tour only, so the story says so and does not invite visits. The TrailChick sentence says it helped open and close Satus, which may be a copy error on the Signal page; the story flags it. The firelookout.com staffing note is undated, and no 2026 status was found. A search summary described a staffing quote from the Yakama fire office; it was not read, so it is not used. The record's height_m of 2.4 looks like the cab width and is proposed as a correction. No new photos: the register's photos are credited to Christine Estrada and no image URLs were read.
